title: NYC Food Protection Certificate Exam
page_numbering: PDF page index (1 = first page of the PDF file); null for HTML pages

questions.question: What does the NYC Health Code require of a food service establishment while it is operating?
options: At least one supervisor certified in food protection on site
All staff to hold a Food Protection Certificate
questions.explanation: At least one certified supervisor must be on site whenever the establishment operates.

source.title: DOHMH: Food Protection Online Course
source.quote: there be at least one supervisor certified in food protection on site any time a food service establishment and non-retail food processing establishment is operating.

questions.question: How many lessons are in DOHMH's free online Food Protection Course?
questions.explanation: The self-paced course has 15 lessons, each followed by a quiz you must pass.

source.title: DOHMH: Food Protection Online Course
source.quote: The course is self-paced and consists of 15 lessons.

questions.question: What is the base price of the in-person final exam after the free online course?
questions.explanation: The online course is free; the in-person exam base price is $24.

source.title: DOHMH: Food Protection Online Course
source.quote: The base price of the exam is $24.

questions.question: How long is a Food Protection Certificate valid?
questions.explanation: The certificate never expires, though DOHMH may require a retake in special circumstances.

source.title: DOHMH Food Protection Course - Online FAQ (PDF)
source.quote: The certificate never expires. There is no need to repeat the course.

questions.question: If you fail an online lesson quiz, what must you do before retaking it?
options: Spend at least 15 consecutive active minutes on the lesson
questions.explanation: You must reopen the lesson and spend at least 15 consecutive active minutes on it.

source.title: DOHMH Food Protection Course - Online FAQ (PDF)
source.quote: spend at least 15 consecutive active minutes on the lesson before you can take the quiz again.

questions.question: How long is the classroom Food Protection Course?
questions.explanation: The classroom course is 15 hours, usually Monday to Friday in 3-hour sessions.

source.title: DOHMH: Food Protection: Classroom
source.quote: The course is 15 hours long and is given over five days and each daily session is three hours long.

questions.question: Which division of the Health Department includes the Health Academy, which provides the Food Protection Course?
options: The Office of the Inspector General
questions.explanation: The Health Academy is an office within the Division of Environmental Health.

source.title: DOHMH Food Protection Course Training Manual (PDF)
source.quote: The Health Academy is an office within the Division of Environmental Health.

questions.question: Is it legal to offer a Health Department sanitarian a gratuity?
options: No; offering any bribe, gratuity or reward for official misconduct is a crime
Yes, if declared on a form
questions.explanation: It is illegal to offer a sanitarian any bribe, gratuity or reward for official misconduct.

source.title: DOHMH Food Protection Course Training Manual (PDF)
source.quote: It is illegal to offer a Sanitarian any bribe, gratuity or reward for official misconduct

questions.question: Who issues the permit every NYC food service establishment must hold?
options: The New York City Health Department
questions.explanation: All food service establishments need a current, valid permit from the NYC Health Department.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: All food service establishments must have a current and valid permit issued by the New York City Health Department.

questions.question: When do health inspectors have the right to inspect a food service establishment?
options: Only during business hours with the owner present
Any time it is operating, with access to all areas
questions.explanation: Inspectors may inspect any operating establishment and must be given access to all areas.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Health inspectors have the right to inspect any operating food service or food processing establishment.

questions.question: Under the NYC Health Code, who in a food service establishment must hold a Food Protection Certificate?
questions.explanation: Supervisors of all food service establishments must have the certificate.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: supervisors of all food service establishments must have a Food Protection Certificate.

questions.question: Which Health Code article regulates the operation of food establishments?
questions.explanation: Article 81 regulates food establishments to prevent public health hazards.

source.title: DOHMH Food Protection Course Training Manual (PDF)
source.quote: Article 81 which regulates the oper- ations of food establishments

questions.question: How does the course define 'food'?
options: Only cooked items sold to customers
Any edible substance, ice, beverage or ingredient used or sold for human consumption
questions.explanation: Ice and beverages count as food.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Food is any edible substance, ice, beverage or ingredient used or sold for human consumption.

questions.question: What are Potentially Hazardous Foods (PHFs)?
options: Foods which support rapid growth of microorganisms
questions.explanation: PHFs support rapid microbial growth.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Potentially Hazardous Foods (PHFs) are foods which support rapid growth of microorganisms.

questions.question: Which of these is listed as a Potentially Hazardous Food?
questions.explanation: PHF examples include cooked rice, pasta, beans, potatoes, tofu and garlic in oil.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: products, fish, shellfish, tofu, cooked rice, pasta, beans, potatoes and garlic in oil.

questions.question: What is ready-to-eat food?
options: Food that has been cooked once
Food that needs no additional heat treatment or washing
questions.explanation: Ready-to-eat food needs no further heating or washing, so extra care is needed.

source.title: DOHMH Food Protection Course Training Manual (PDF)
source.quote: Any food product that does not need additional heat treatment or washing is called ready-to-eat food.

questions.question: From whom must all foods be purchased?
questions.explanation: All foods must come from approved sources that comply with production rules.

source.title: DOHMH Food Protection Course Training Manual (PDF)
source.quote: All foods must be purchased from approved sources.

questions.question: What is the Temperature Danger Zone?
questions.explanation: Most harmful microorganisms reproduce rapidly between 41°F and 140°F.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: The Temperature Danger Zone is between 41°F and 140°F.

questions.question: At or below what temperature must cold foods be held (other than smoked fish)?
questions.explanation: Cold foods are held at or below 41°F; smoked fish at or below 38°F.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: All cold foods must be held at or below 41°F (except smoked fish, which must be held at or below 38°F) at all times.

questions.question: Smoked fish must be held at or below what temperature?
questions.explanation: Smoked fish is held at or below 38°F to prevent growth of Clostridium botulinum.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Smoked fish must be held at or below 38°F to prevent the growth of the bacteria Clostridium botulinum.

questions.question: At what temperature must frozen foods be kept?
questions.explanation: Frozen foods must be kept frozen at 0°F or lower.

source.title: DOHMH Food Protection Course Training Manual (PDF)
source.quote: Keep frozen foods frozen at 0° F or lower.

questions.question: At what temperature must hot foods in a hot holding unit be held?
questions.explanation: Hot holding requires 140°F or higher.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: All hot foods stored in a hot holding unit must be held at 140°F or higher.

questions.question: If potentially hazardous foods are left in the Temperature Danger Zone for more than how long, must they be discarded?
questions.explanation: After more than 2 hours in the danger zone, the food is no longer safe.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: If potentially hazardous foods are left in the Temperature Danger Zone for more than 2 hours, then the food is no longer safe

questions.question: Where should a refrigeration thermometer be placed?
options: On the outside of the door
In the warmest spot in the unit
In the coldest spot in the unit
questions.explanation: Place it in the warmest spot to measure the unit's ambient air temperature.

source.title: DOHMH Food Protection Course Training Manual (PDF)
source.quote: Place a refrigeration thermometer in the warmest spot in the unit to measure ambient air temperature of the unit

questions.question: Which type of thermometer is prohibited in a food service establishment?
questions.explanation: Glass thermometers are prohibited by law.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: The use of glass thermometers in a food service establishment is prohibited by law.

questions.question: What is the temperature range of a bimetallic stem thermometer?
questions.explanation: Bimetallic stem thermometers range from 0°F to 220°F.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: bimetallic stem (range from 0°F to 220°F), thermocouple and thermistor (digital).

questions.question: A thermistor thermometer is commonly called what?
questions.explanation: The thermistor has a digital readout and is commonly called a digital thermometer.

source.title: DOHMH Food Protection Course Training Manual (PDF)
source.quote: there is a thermometer called thermistor, which has a digital read out and is commonly called "digital thermometer."

questions.question: How accurate is a bimetallic stem thermometer, per the Training Manual?
questions.explanation: The bi-metallic stem is accurate to within 2°F and easy to re-calibrate.

source.title: DOHMH Food Protection Course Training Manual (PDF)
source.quote: accurate to + or – 2°F and easy to re-calibrate.

questions.question: In the ice-point calibration method, what temperature should a thermometer read in a 50/50 ice-water slush?
questions.explanation: A 50/50 ice water slush is always 32°F at sea level; adjust the hex nut if the reading is off.

source.title: DOHMH Food Protection Course Training Manual (PDF)
source.quote: If the temperature is 32°F, do nothing, the thermometer is accurate.

questions.question: Where should the thermometer probe be inserted to measure a food's internal temperature?
options: The thickest part or the center of the product
questions.explanation: Insert into the thickest part or the center, ideally at several points.

source.title: DOHMH Food Protection Course Training Manual (PDF)
source.quote: Measure the internal product temperature by inserting the probe into the thickest part or the center of the product.

questions.question: Meat inspected by the USDA must bear what?
questions.explanation: USDA-inspected meat must have a USDA inspection stamp.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: must have a USDA inspection stamp.

questions.question: How long must shellfish tags be kept on file?
options: At least 90 days after the product is used
questions.explanation: Shellfish tags are kept at least 90 days after the product is used.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: These tags must be kept on file for at least 90 days after the product is used.

questions.question: What sell-by dating applies to pasteurized milk?
questions.explanation: Pasteurized milk has a 9-day sell-by; ultra-pasteurized has 45 days.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Milk and milk products must either be pasteurized, with sell-by dates of 9 days, or ultra-pasteurized, with sell-by dates of 45 days.

questions.question: What sell-by dating applies to ultra-pasteurized milk products?
questions.explanation: Ultra-pasteurized products carry 45-day sell-by dates.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: ultra-pasteurized, with sell-by dates of 45 days.

questions.question: When receiving, which canned goods should you look out for and reject?
options: Dented, leaking, rusted or swollen cans
questions.explanation: Reject dented, leaking, rusted or swollen cans.

source.title: DOHMH Food Protection Course Training Manual (PDF)
source.quote: Look out for any dented, leaking, rusted or swollen cans.

questions.question: What color should fresh beef be when received?
questions.explanation: Beef should be bright to dark red with no objectionable odor.

source.title: DOHMH Food Protection Course Training Manual (PDF)
source.quote: Beef should be bright to dark red in color with no objection- able odor.

questions.question: What must be done with all fruits and vegetables that will be served raw?
questions.explanation: Raw-served produce must be thoroughly washed.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: All fruits and vegetables served raw must be thoroughly washed before being served.

questions.question: Is vacuum packaging food allowed in a retail food establishment?
options: No, unless special authorization is obtained from the Health Department
Yes, if labeled with a date
questions.explanation: Vacuum packaging is prohibited unless the Health Department specially authorizes it.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Vacuum packaging of any food product in a retail food establishment is prohibited by law unless special authorization is obtained

questions.question: How must commercial foods in modified atmosphere packaging be used?
options: Within 24 hours of opening regardless of label
questions.explanation: Modified atmosphere packaged foods must be used per manufacturer's specifications.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: All commercial foods in modified atmosphere packaging must be used per manufacturer’s specifications.

questions.question: What does FIFO stand for?
questions.explanation: FIFO means First In First Out; the first step is dating the products.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: FIFO means First In First Out.

questions.question: What is the first step in implementing the FIFO method?
questions.explanation: Dating products is the first step of FIFO.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: The first step in implementing the FIFO method is to date the products.

questions.question: How high off the floor must food items be stored?
questions.explanation: The Health Code requires all food to be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: The New York City Health Code requires that all food items be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.

questions.question: In a refrigerator, where must raw foods be stored relative to cooked foods?
options: On the same shelf, side by side
questions.explanation: Storing raw below cooked prevents cross-contamination.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: In order to prevent cross-contamination, raw foods in a refrigerator must be stored below cooked foods.

questions.question: Storing raw meats from bottom to top, which goes on the bottom shelf?
questions.explanation: Bottom to top: poultry, ground meats, pork, then all other meats.

source.title: DOHMH Food Protection Course Training Manual (PDF)
source.quote: Store raw meats in the following order from bottom to top: i. Poultry ii. Ground meats iii. Pork iv. All other meats

questions.question: What dry storage conditions does the manual strongly recommend?
options: Humidity of 50% and a temperature of 70°F
questions.explanation: Dry storage: 50% humidity and 70°F are strongly recommended.

source.title: DOHMH Food Protection Course Training Manual (PDF)
source.quote: Humidity of 50% and a temperature of 70° F are strongly recommended.

questions.question: Where must food never be stored?
options: On shelves 6 inches off the floor
questions.explanation: Never store foods under wastewater lines.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Never store foods under wastewater lines.

questions.question: Can ice intended for human consumption be used to chill cans and bottles?
options: Yes, if the cans are washed
Yes, if it is changed daily
questions.explanation: Ice for consumption cannot be used to store cans, bottles or other food products.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Ice intended for human consumption cannot be used for storing cans, bottles or other food products.

questions.question: When food is stored directly in ice, what must happen to the meltwater?
options: It can stay until the end of the shift
questions.explanation: Water from the ice must be drained constantly.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: When foods are stored directly in ice, the water from that ice must be drained constantly.

questions.question: How must stored food be kept?
options: In plastic bags on the floor
questions.explanation: Stored food must be covered and kept in vermin-proof containers.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Stored food must be kept covered and stored in vermin-proof containers.

questions.question: Where must the 'First Aid Choking' poster be posted?
options: In a conspicuous place in each designated eating area
questions.explanation: It must be posted visibly in each designated eating area.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: The "First Aid Choking" poster must be posted in a visible (conspicuous) place in each designated eating area.

questions.question: Which establishments must display the 'Alcohol and Pregnancy Warning' sign?
questions.explanation: Establishments serving alcohol must display the sign.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Food service establishments which serve alcoholic beverages are required to display the "Alcohol and Pregnancy Warning" sign.

questions.question: Where must a 'Wash Hands' sign be displayed?
questions.explanation: A 'Wash Hands' sign is required at every hand washing sink.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: A "Wash Hands" sign must be displayed at all hand washing sinks.

questions.question: What are the three main hazards to health in food?
questions.explanation: Hazards are physical, chemical and biological.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: There are three main hazards to our health: physical, chemical and biological.

questions.question: Glass fragments found in food are which type of hazard?
questions.explanation: Foreign objects such as glass or metal are physical hazards.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: The presence of a foreign object (e.g., glass fragments, pieces of metal) in a food is considered a physical hazard.

questions.question: Cleaning agents in food are which type of hazard?
questions.explanation: Pesticides, cleaning agents and medicine in food are chemical hazards.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: The presence of harmful chemicals (e.g., pesticide, cleaning agents, prescription medicine) in a food is called a chemical hazard.

questions.question: Bacteria, viruses, parasites and fungi in food are which type of hazard?
questions.explanation: Microorganisms in food are biological hazards.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: The presence of microorganisms (bacteria, viruses, parasites and fungi) in a food is called a biological hazard.

questions.question: Can you tell by sight, taste or smell whether food is contaminated with pathogenic bacteria?
options: No; contaminated food often looks, tastes and smells normal
questions.explanation: Food contaminated with pathogens often shows no change in appearance, taste or smell.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: there is no change in appearance, taste or smell.

questions.question: Under favorable conditions, how often can the number of bacteria in food double?
questions.explanation: Bacteria can double every 20 to 30 minutes.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Under favorable conditions the number of bacteria in a food can double every 20 to 30 minutes.

questions.question: In which phase of bacterial growth does the most rapid growth occur?
questions.explanation: The four phases are lag, log, stationary and death; growth is fastest in the log phase.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: The most rapid growth of bacteria takes place in the log phase.

questions.question: What does the acronym FATTOM stand for?
options: Food, Acidity, Temperature, Time, Oxygen, Moisture
Fat, Acid, Toxin, Temperature, Odor, Mold
Food, Air, Taste, Texture, Odor, Mass
Freezing, Aging, Thawing, Tasting, Opening, Mixing
questions.explanation: FATTOM lists the six factors affecting bacterial growth.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Six factors affect the growth of bacteria: Food, Acidity, Temperature, Time, Oxygen and Moisture (FATTOM).

questions.question: Can viruses reproduce in food?
options: Yes, only in the danger zone
No, but they can be transmitted to people through food
questions.explanation: Viruses cannot reproduce in food but can be transmitted through it.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Viruses cannot reproduce in food. However, viruses can be transmitted to people if they get into food.

questions.question: Which two common food-borne viruses are spread by food or water contaminated with an infected person's feces?
questions.explanation: Proper handwashing after using the toilet prevents transmission.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Hepatitis A and norovirus are two common food-borne viruses.

questions.question: Trichinella spiralis, which causes trichinosis, is typically found in which food?
questions.explanation: Trichinella is a parasite in under-cooked pork; cook pork to 150°F for 15 seconds.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Trichinella spiralis, which causes trichinosis, is a food-borne parasite typically found in under-cooked pork.

questions.question: Anisakis simplex is a parasite typically found in what?
questions.explanation: Anisakis simplex is a food-borne parasite of marine fish.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Anisakis simplex is a food-borne parasite typically found in marine fish.

questions.question: Salmonella enteritidis is commonly found in which foods?
options: Raw poultry and raw shell eggs
questions.explanation: Salmonella enteritidis is common in raw poultry and raw shell eggs.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Salmonella enteritidis is a bacterium commonly found in raw poultry and raw shell eggs.

questions.question: How can the growth of Clostridium perfringens be controlled?
options: Rapid cooling, rapid reheating and avoiding preparing foods in advance
questions.explanation: C. perfringens is controlled by rapid cooling and reheating and not preparing food far in advance.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Clostridium perfringens by rapid cooling, rapid reheating and by avoiding preparation of foods in advance.

questions.question: Which bacterium is commonly carried by healthy people?
questions.explanation: Staphylococcus aureus is commonly carried by healthy human beings.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Staphylococcus aureus is a bacterium that is commonly carried by healthy human beings.

questions.question: How can staphylococcal food intoxication be prevented?
options: Good personal hygiene and avoiding bare-hand contact with ready-to-eat foods
questions.explanation: Good hygiene and no bare-hand contact with RTE foods prevent it.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: which can be prevented by good personal hygiene and avoiding bare hand contact with ready-to-eat foods.

questions.question: Ground meat must be cooked to what minimum temperature to eliminate E. coli 0157:H7?
questions.explanation: Ground meat must reach at least 158°F.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Ground meat (e.g., hamburgers) must be cooked to a minimum temperature of 158°F to eliminate E. coli 0157:H7.

questions.question: Clostridium botulinum, the cause of botulism, is associated with which foods?
options: Home-canned foods, smoked fish and garlic in oil
questions.explanation: C. botulinum is associated with home-canned foods, smoked fish, garlic in oil and anaerobic environments.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: It is associated with home-canned foods, smoked fish, garlic in oil and any food in an anaerobic

questions.question: Scombroid poisoning comes from eating which fish after time and temperature abuse?
options: Fish with high histamine levels such as tuna and mackerel
questions.explanation: Scombroid poisoning involves fish like tuna, mackerel, bonito, mahi mahi and bluefish.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Scombroid poisoning occurs from eating certain fish with high levels of histamines (e.g., tuna, mackerel, bonito, mahi mahi, bluefish)

questions.question: Should a food worker with an illness transmissible through food come to work?
options: Yes, if only working the register
questions.explanation: Workers with transmissible illnesses should not work until fully recovered.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Food workers with an illness that can be transmitted by contact with food or through food should not work until fully recovered.

questions.question: Within what distance of food preparation areas must hand washing sinks be readily accessible?
questions.explanation: Sinks must be within 25 feet of food prep areas and in or near all toilets.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: hand washing sinks to be readily accessible within 25 feet of all food preparation areas and in or near all toilets.

questions.question: What must a hand washing sink be provided with?
options: Soap, hot and cold running water, disposable towels or a hand dryer, and a 'Wash Hands' sign
questions.explanation: All four items are required.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: The hand washing sinks must be provided with soap, hot and cold running water, disposable towels or a hand dryer and a "Wash Hands" sign.

questions.question: What jewelry may food workers wear on their arms and hands?
options: Only wedding bands and medical bracelets
questions.explanation: No jewelry on arms and hands except wedding bands and medical bracelets.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: not wear any jewelry on their arms and hands (except for wedding bands and medical bracelets).

questions.question: Is a common sink allowed for both food preparation and hand washing?
questions.explanation: Using a common sink for food prep or equipment washing as well as hand washing is not permitted.

source.title: DOHMH Food Protection Course Training Manual (PDF)
source.quote: The use of a common sink for food preparation or for washing equipment and/or utensils as well for hand washing is not permitted.

questions.question: Do gloves replace hand washing?
options: No, gloves are never a replacement for good hand washing
Yes, if they are fabric gloves
questions.explanation: Gloves never replace hand washing; wash before putting them on.

source.title: DOHMH Food Protection Course Training Manual (PDF)
source.quote: The use of gloves is never a replacement for good hand washing practices!

questions.question: Which gloves may NOT be used with ready-to-eat food?
questions.explanation: Fabric or reusable gloves may not be used with ready-to-eat food.

source.title: DOHMH Food Protection Course Training Manual (PDF)
source.quote: Fabric or re-usable gloves may not be used with ready-to-eat (RTE) food.

questions.question: What should you do with gloves if food preparation is interrupted?
options: Remove and discard them, then wash hands before using clean gloves
questions.explanation: Remove and discard gloves on interruption; wash hands and use clean gloves when resuming.

source.title: DOHMH Food Protection Course Training Manual (PDF)
source.quote: If an interruption occurs during food preparation, remove gloves and discard.

questions.question: Which is an acceptable way to thaw frozen food?
options: On the counter at room temperature
In a sink of hot water
questions.explanation: Acceptable methods include refrigeration, cold running water, and microwave followed by continuous cooking. Never thaw at room temperature.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: refrigerating them, placing them under cold running water, or defrosting them in a microwave oven with continuous cooking afterwards.

questions.question: Should frozen food ever be thawed at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Never thaw frozen food at room temperature, and never re-freeze thawed food.

source.title: DOHMH Food Protection Course Training Manual (PDF)
source.quote: Never thaw frozen food at room temperature.

questions.question: What is cross contamination?
options: Cooking two foods in one pan
When bacteria from a raw food get into a cooked or ready-to-eat food
questions.explanation: Cross contamination is transfer from raw to cooked or ready-to-eat food.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Cross contamination occurs when bacteria from a raw food get into a cooked or ready-to-eat food.

questions.question: To what internal temperature must poultry, stuffed meat and stuffing be cooked?
questions.explanation: Poultry, stuffed meat and stuffing must reach 165°F.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Poultry, stuffed meat and stuffing must be cooked to an internal temperature of 165°F.

questions.question: To what internal temperature must pork be cooked?
questions.explanation: Pork must reach 150°F.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Pork must be cooked to an internal temperature of 150°F.

questions.question: To what minimum temperature must raw shell eggs be cooked?
questions.explanation: Raw shell eggs must be cooked to at least 145°F.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Raw shell eggs must be cooked to a minimum temperature of 145°F.

questions.question: To what minimum temperature must fish, shellfish, beef and lamb be cooked?
questions.explanation: Fish, shellfish, beef, lamb and all other meats: 140°F minimum.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Fish, shellfish, beef, lamb and all other meats must be cooked to a minimum temperature of 140°F.

questions.question: To what temperature must previously cooked, refrigerated foods be reheated for hot holding?
options: 165°F, rapidly, using a stove or oven
questions.explanation: Reheat rapidly to 165°F on a stove or in an oven; never reheat in a hot holding unit.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: must be rapidly reheated to 165°F using a stove or an oven.

questions.question: Can a hot holding unit be used to reheat foods?
questions.explanation: Never use a hot holding unit to reheat foods.

source.title: DOHMH Online Food Protection Course Study Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Never use a hot holding unit to reheat foods.

questions.question: Within what time must previously cooked foods be reheated to 165°F, per the Training Manual?
questions.explanation: Inadequate reheating means not reaching 165°F within two hours using a stove or oven.

source.title: DOHMH Food Protection Course Training Manual (PDF)
